profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Provincial Legal Bureau and an external public-law consultant supporting the SIDa roadmap package for Banten, West Sumatera, and Bali. The immediate context is that the province wants to align the legal drafting workstream with the policy and stakeholder-mapping workstream before circulating documents to district/city governments and the governor's office. The agenda is to confirm which documents are moving this week, how the legal basis section will be assembled, which annexes and matrices are being handed off between teams, and how district/city input will be requested. The expected outcome is apparent alignment on deliverables, handoffs, and timing for circulation of the SIDa roadmap package, without explicitly reopening underlying assumptions.

members.name: Rina Prasetyo
members.role: Head of Regional Regulation Drafting Subdivision, Provincial Legal Bureau
members.expertise: Provincial administrative law, legal harmonization, governor regulations, internal clearance procedures
members.background: A career government lawyer who has spent twelve years coordinating draft gubernatorial instruments and inter-agency legal reviews for provincial programs.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid sending anything upward that will be rejected for procedural incompleteness, and she is trying to keep the governor's office comfortable by making the SIDa package look administratively settled before formal circulation.
hidden_assumptions: When colleagues say a draft is 'final,' they usually mean it has already passed internal legal cleanup and is ready for formal circulation outside the working team.

The 'legal basis' for a roadmap package should include every instrument needed for implementation architecture, including the governor decree for the coordination team and any supporting formal cooperation instruments.
If district/city input is requested, it should go through the province's formal outgoing-letter channel so the responses can later be cited in the legal file.
The working reference point is the latest annotated bundle on the Legal Bureau shared drive, because that is the version tied to internal harmonization notes.

members.name: Arief Mahendra
members.role: Senior Public Policy Counsel, Nusantara Governance Advisory
members.expertise: Decentralization law, policy-roadmap drafting, comparative provincial governance frameworks, stakeholder coordination
members.background: A former university governance researcher who now advises provincial governments on turning innovation-policy studies into legally usable planning documents.
members.private_state: He wants to keep momentum by getting a workable package out quickly to the provinces and districts, and he is trying to protect the study team from getting pulled into formal bureaucratic steps too early.
hidden_assumptions: When a client asks for a 'final draft,' they usually mean the last consultant working draft before comments from districts and the governor's office come in.
The 'legal basis' section of the roadmap should be limited to currently valid normative references that justify the roadmap, not future implementing instruments that will be drafted afterward.
Getting district/city input can start informally through Bappeda focal points by email or WhatsApp, because the purpose at this stage is substantive feedback rather than record perfection.
The operative version is the clean consultant file dated after the Bali workshop, because comments made in the shared drive before that were largely superseded.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to sending the 'final draft' this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a legally cleaned, internally harmonized draft that is ready to be formally circulated to the governor's office and external agencies.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the consultant's last integrated working version that is stable enough to collect stakeholder comments but still expected to change afterward.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal-policy coordination, 'final draft' is commonly used as a routine milestone label, so each person hears a familiar bureaucratic phrase and assumes the other is using the same stage convention.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the 'legal basis' section
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the package needs a complete 'legal basis' before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes existing statutes plus the draft governor decree establishing the provincial SIDa coordination team and other implementation-enabling instruments needed to make the roadmap operable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes only enacted national, provincial, and planning-law references that justify the roadmap's authority, while treating team-establishment and cooperation instruments as later follow-on documents.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to saying 'legal basis' as a standard section heading, and neither expects that the other draws the boundary differently because the phrase sounds settled and technical.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss updating 'the matrix' before handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the Legal Bureau's crosswalk matrix linking each SIDa roadmap section to supporting regulations, internal reviewers, and required formal attachments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the consultant team's comparative matrix of provincial readiness elements across Banten, West Sumatera, and Bali, including commodities, HR, and institutional gaps.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams have been using a spreadsheet called 'matrix' for weeks, and in fast coordination meetings neither side naturally restates the filename or content because each assumes there is only one salient matrix at this stage.

misalignment_points.topic: How district/city comments will be requested
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'circulate to districts for comments' after the package is ready.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the province will send a formal signed letter through the administrative channel, with attached draft documents and a response deadline that becomes part of the legal record.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes he can first email or message district Bappeda contacts an editable draft for quick substantive comments, and formal letters can follow later if needed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The substantive goal sounds identical and both methods are common in practice, so the phrase 'circulate for comments' creates an illusion of agreement while hiding different assumptions about channel, traceability, and document control.

turns.inner_thought: I need this SIDa package to move only if it is administratively safe. For me, this week means we should be locking the set that can go upward without Legal Bureau being told it is premature. I need to hear what Arief is actually handing over so I can line it up against the annotated bundle on the shared drive and see whether the package is ready for formal circulation.

turns.inner_thought: The consultant version is already stable enough after the Bali workshop. I do not want us dragged into full bureaucratic processing before we get practical reactions from districts and the governor's office. When she says move this week, I assume she means we can send the last integrated working version. I mainly need agreement on what annexes travel with it and in what order we collect comments.

I will say 'complete legal basis' because that should be obvious.

turns.utterance: All right. Once those pieces are in, we can circulate to districts for comments. I want the package to look settled when it leaves the province, so we do not create avoidable questions later.
